title: skill-evals: a turn inherits the host's memory variables, so project memory reaches both arms of a round
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

Filing gate: ① (a defect a card thread measured while running the eval for #37796) · Source: fleet (PR #37841)

## What happens

`turnEnv` in `packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/run.ts` passes the host's whole environment to every eval turn, minus the API-billing and effort variables. When the runner is started inside a project container, the memory variables (`CLAUDE_COWORK_MEMORY_PATH_OVERRIDE`, `CLAUDE_MEMORY_STORES`) go through too. Each turn then reads the project's memory in both arms. In the first round for PR #37841, all three without-skill answers to case 2 quoted a project memory note about the very change the case tests, so the without-skill arm scored as if it had the skill. With those two variables removed, the second round was clean: case 2 scored 3/3 with the skill and 0/3 without.

## Expected

An eval turn sees only what its arm gives it: the skill or no skill, never the host's memory. `turnEnv` drops every memory variable the CLI reads, and the round's record says the turn environment was scrubbed.

## Done when

- [ ] `turnEnv` removes the memory variables, listed in one place next to the billing and effort ones.
- [ ] A test pins it: a host env carrying the memory variables yields a turn env without them.
- [ ] The README of the runner says a round run inside a project container is isolated from project memory.

Grade: area:ai · bug · reach: any skill-eval round run from a project container; it inflates the without-skill arm and hides a skill's value · evidence: measured (two rounds of PR #37841, before and after removing the variables)
Suggested-grade: p2
Size: S
Related: PR #37841, #37796.
